orientation.theorem: For simple spectra, stationarity of -Tr(A U B Udagger) gives [A,U B Udagger]=0. Global minimum pairs eigenvalues in the same order (trace rearrangement); all stationary orientations are permutations, with no mixing. Separate-sector spectral potentials leave all orientations flat.
orientation.implication: A spectral mass potential or a single linear mixed trace cannot select observed mixing. Competing orientation invariants are required; their coefficients must be derived rather than fitted.

lepton_branches.supplied_scale: Delta m31²=.0025 eV², subtraction mu=1eV; not derived
lepton_branches.allowed_counterterm: c Tr[(Mnu† Mnu)^2] is weak-basis invariant and CP even; its coefficient is an unspecified UV scalar-potential matching datum
lepton_branches.conclusion: One-loop neutrino vacuum energy does not select a physical lepton phase from these fitted roots without fixing the allowed invariant counterterm. A chosen subtraction convention is not a dynamical prediction.
lepton_branches.prior: TOE51 already owns branch-dependent masses and m_bb;11960 owns the fitted roots. This audits a proposed dynamical ranking.

Majorana_sensitive_positive_control.exact_orientation_potential: For S=U_R U_R.T, t=|S11|²=|S22|², I_R=2 y1² y2²+t(y1²-y2²)². Positive coefficient selects t=0 globally on the2D unitary orbit.
Majorana_sensitive_positive_control.boundary: Known O2-right-handed Majorana orientation mechanism, not a newly discovered flavour theorem. Singular values and degenerate heavy mass are supplied. The exact light masses are degenerate, so the displayed45-degree Takagi basis does not predict an observable mixing angle;3-family splitting, coefficient selection and UV embedding remain open.

scope: Executed two concrete selector candidates and their obstructions. No unique flavour coefficients, mass scale or out-of-sample selected branch derived.
